neighbours.label: an opening parenthesis that starts an aside inside a noun phrase, between determiner/modifier and noun (his (essentially ...) defence)
fire: We finally tried their (rather expensive) tasting menu on Friday night.
He defended his (admittedly unusual) theory in front of the committee.
She showed off her (slightly burnt) apple pie at the family dinner.
The band played their (mostly forgotten) second album from start to finish.
I was impressed by the (surprisingly quiet) engine of the new truck.
They moved into a (very small) apartment above the corner bakery.
Thanks to my (limited) knowledge of Spanish, we found the station.
The museum displays a (supposedly cursed) mask from the old temple.
quiet: We finally tried their tasting menu on Friday night (it was rather expensive).
He defended his theory in front of the committee, though it was unusual.
She showed off her apple pie at the family dinner (made on Sunday).
The band played their second album from start to finish (released in 1998).
I was impressed by how quiet the engine of the new truck was.
They moved into an apartment above the corner bakery (on Main Street).
Thanks to my knowledge of Spanish, which is limited, we found the station.
The museum displays an old mask from the temple (see the photo below).
